title: STEPHEN (Tries to move off.) Will some one tell me where I am least likely to meet these necessary evils?
html_source:
Chapter 9, “Scylla and Charybdis”

—A father, Stephen said, battling against hopelessness, is a necessary evil.

Stephen considers himself under the oppression of two figurative fathers in addition to his biological father Simon: the imperial British rule and the Catholic Church. Earlier in “Circe,” Stephen drunkenly verbalizes his opposition to both:

(He taps his brow.) But in here it is I must kill the priest and the king.
